---
title: "Troubleshooting and model choice"
---

| Symptom | First checks and actions |
|---|---|
| Data validation fails | Check the reported columns and run identities. Confirm complete grids, constant inputs and unique group/rep/time keys. Do not pad or drop observations without a scientific decision. |
| Too few groups for a split | Reduce requested partitions explicitly or produce more scenarios. Replicates are not substitutes for independent parameter groups. |
| Non-finite loss | Inspect numeric ranges and model options. Try a smaller learning rate and a small baseline. Constant dimensions are already handled; do not add noise just to hide a failure. |
| Good training loss, poor validation | Compare parameter coverage and model capacity; tune using validation, and use early stopping with an explicit patience. |
| Good transformer training loss, poor predictions | Inspect autonomous rollouts. Teacher-forced next-step loss can hide accumulating prediction errors. |
| Good average, missing stochastic variability | A deterministic model cannot generate a conditional distribution. Compare flow matching or iTARFlow on distributional metrics. |
| Negative counts or broken conservation | Inspect violation reports. The models do not enforce these rules. A support-aware model or transformation is a separate scientific decision. |
| CUDA unavailable | Use `device="cpu"` or choose a compatible CUDA PyTorch index and driver using the quickstart. An installed CUDA wheel alone does not guarantee a usable GPU. |
| Out of memory | Reduce batch size, width, sequence length or sample batch size as appropriate. The bank still needs RAM even though training uses device minibatches. |
| Reloaded predictions differ | Use the complete artifact, same sampling seed and numerical settings. Old raw checkpoints lack preprocessing. |
| Conditioning is missing or shape is wrong | Supply `(B,T,K)` original-unit values in `observed_outputs` order; do not pass changing data as static inputs. Evaluation banks need the full original output schema. |
| Resume reports a mismatch | Reuse the exact bank, split, architecture, scaling, total steps and numerical/topology settings. A changed experiment starts a new fit; an inference artifact is not an optimizer checkpoint. |
| Precision or compilation fails | Recheck hardware support; try `precision=fp32` and `compile_model=false`. TF32 needs CUDA; compile and deterministic modes cannot be combined. Record the numerical mode actually used. |
| Multiprocess startup fails | Guard Python script entry with `if __name__ == "__main__":`; ensure global batch size divides the worker count and requested CUDA devices exist. |
| Inference looks overconfident | Check identifiability, observation assumptions, surrogate fidelity and posterior predictive calibration. More flow samples do not measure surrogate-error uncertainty. |

Start with an MLP and a train-mean baseline. Use a transformer if sequential
structure is useful; compare whole-rollout error. Use flow matching when
stochastic trajectories matter. Use iTARFlow when a tractable density is useful
and the continuous support assumptions are defensible.

Presets are starting configurations, not automatic recommendations. Learning
rate, data coverage, sample budget and the scientific target can matter more
than the model family. The architecture pages give more detail; the package evaluation workflow
provides common diagnostics.
